root_cause.text: The `__rdma_block_iter_next()` function in `drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c` uses 32-bit `unsigned int` local variables (`block_offset` and `delta`) to calculate DMA addresses, which causes an integer overflow when handling block sizes of 4GB or larger.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the types of `block_offset` and `delta` in `__rdma_block_iter_next()` are changed from `unsigned int` to `dma_addr_t` to prevent truncation and overflow when reassembling split SG entries.

intent_record.what: Changed the data types of local variables 'block_offset' and 'delta' from 'unsigned int' to 'dma_addr_t' in the '__rdma_block_iter_next' function.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that DMA address offsets and deltas are stored in a type wide enough to prevent truncation or overflow on systems with 64-bit DMA addresses.

RDMA: Move DMA block iterator logic into dedicated files

The DMA iterator logic was mixed into verbs and umem-specific
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 6094ea64c69520ed1e770e7c79c43412de202bfa
Author: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Feb 13 12:57:37 2026 +0200

    RDMA: Move DMA block iterator logic into dedicated files
    
    The DMA iterator logic was mixed into verbs and umem-specific code,
    forcing all users to include rdma/ib_umem.h. Move the block iterator
    logic into iter.c and rdma/iter.h so that rdma/ib_umem.h and
    rdma/ib_verbs.h can be separated in a follow-up patch.
    
    Link: https://patch.msgid.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function `__rdma_block_iter_next` declares `block_offset` and `delta` as 32-bit `unsigned int` variables on lines 22-23. When the block size is 4GB or larger (i.e., `biter->__pg_bit` >= 32), `BIT_ULL(biter->__pg_bit)` will be `0x100000000` or larger, which exceeds the capacity of a 32-bit integer, causing an integer overflow during the calculation of `block_offset` and `delta` on lines 29-30.
